items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: Lil Armstrong and Dutrey was in the band.

ctx.x: Oh, I see. Then King Oliver was obviously the first.

That came from -- now Bubber was playing with Mamie Smith like Johnny Dunn with the plunger doing the wawa -- wa wa wa wa -- but King Oliver had a growl with the mute that came with cornet. In those days they didn't play trumpets, they played cornets. All the New Orleans boys played cornets. The easterners played trumpets. And Bubber got that growl, because every night after we finished up the show we would go to the Dreamland and sit there and listen to Johnny Dodds and Baby Dodds and King Oliver. Louis wasn't…

created in New York by New York musicians. Bubber was a New Yorker and so was Charlie Ervin, and those were the two guys that put the growl in Duke's band that gave him his style. Two New Yorkers, not southerners or westerners, they were New Yorkers. Two New York born boys. Bubber was born down in Hell's Kitchen and I think Charlie Ervis was born not too far from there. Both New Yorkers, and Duke's style came from a New York style of playing -- the growl. You see, the growl was developed, you know, King Oliver…
